prompt: What is the mass of an electron?
explanation: The electron mass is 9.11 x 10^-31 kg, about 1836 times smaller than the proton’s 1.67 x 10^-27 kg. It appears in the radius of a circular path, r = mv/(qB), and in the cyclotron frequency.

why.b: Wrong. That is the PROTON mass, which is far larger.
why.c: Wrong. That is the elementary charge, in coulombs not kilograms.
why.d: Wrong sign on the exponent, which would make an electron heavier than a star.

prompt: The electron mass is 9.11 times 10 to the power minus {{1}} kg.
explanation: Minus 31. The proton, at 10 to the minus 27, is about two thousand times heavier.

prompt: What is the mass of a proton?
explanation: The proton mass is 1.67 x 10^-27 kg. Keep the three small constants apart by their exponents: charge at 10 to the minus 19 C, proton at 10 to the minus 27 kg, electron at 10 to the minus 31 kg.

why.b: Wrong. That is the electron mass.
why.c: Wrong. That is a charge, not a mass.

prompt: The proton mass is 1.67 times 10 to the power minus {{1}} kg.
In F = qvB sin theta, name TWO situations in which a charged particle in a magnetic field feels no force at all.

options.text: When it is stationary, and when it moves along the field direction
When it is stationary, and when it moves at 90 degrees to the field
When it moves fast, and when the field is strong
When the charge is negative, and when the field is uniform
There is no situation in which the force vanishes

explanation: Two ways to make the product zero. If v = 0 the whole expression is zero, so a stationary charge feels nothing. If theta = 0 the particle moves ALONG the field and sin 0 = 0, so again nothing. The force is greatest at 90 degrees, where the sine is 1.

why.a: Correct. Either no motion, or motion parallel to the field.
why.b: Wrong on the second: 90 degrees is where the force is at its MAXIMUM.
why.c: Wrong. Both of those increase the force.
why.d: Wrong. A negative charge feels a force in the opposite direction, not no force.
why.e: Wrong. Both cases above give exactly zero.

prompt: A charge moving ALONG a magnetic field feels no force, because sin 0 equals {{1}}.
explanation: Zero. The angle is measured between the velocity and the field, so moving along the field kills the force entirely.

prompt: What happens to the kinetic energy of a charged particle moving through a magnetic field alone?

options.text: It stays constant, because a magnetic field steers but never speeds up
It oscillates between zero and a maximum
It depends on the sign of the charge

explanation: The magnetic force is always perpendicular to the velocity, and a force at right angles to the motion does no work. So the speed, and with it the kinetic energy, is unchanged: the field only changes the DIRECTION. That is why the path is a circle at constant speed.

why.a: Correct. Magnetic fields steer, they do not accelerate in the sense of changing speed.
why.b: Wrong. That would require work to be done, which a perpendicular force cannot do.
why.d: Wrong. The speed is constant throughout.
why.e: Wrong. The sign changes which way it curves, not the speed.

prompt: A magnetic field can increase the speed of a charged particle.
explanation: It cannot. The magnetic force is always perpendicular to the velocity, so it does no work and cannot change the speed. It changes direction only.

why.true: Wrong. A perpendicular force does no work, so the kinetic energy cannot rise.
why.false: Correct. Magnetic fields steer but never speed up.

prompt: What is notable about the cyclotron frequency f = qB / (2 pi m)?

options.text: It contains no v, so the frequency does not depend on the particle’s speed
It rises in proportion to the speed
It falls in proportion to the speed
It depends on the radius but not on the field

explanation: No v appears in the formula. A faster particle travels a larger circle, since r = mv/(qB), and the two effects cancel exactly, so it goes round in the same time. That is the cyclotron principle, and it is what makes the machine work with a fixed driving frequency.

why.a: Correct, and the cancellation with the radius is why.
why.d: Wrong. B is in the formula and r is not.
why.e: Wrong. It holds for any charged particle.

prompt: The cyclotron frequency is independent of the particle’s {{1}}.
explanation: Speed. The charge, the mass and the field all appear in f = qB/(2 pi m); the speed does not.
